deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is the Lego-Teichmüller project of 1983, worked out for genus 0 with five marked points: M_{0,5} with the symmetric group S_K (|K| = 5, order 120) acting by relabelling. The facing page (33) classifies 'special' 5-point configurations on P^1, i.e. those with a non-trivial automorphism. They are the cyclic pentagon (automorphism group D5, the S5-orbit has 120/10 = 12 elements), the square pyramid (Z/4, orbit 30), the equilateral bipyramid (D3, orbit 20), and so on. These are the orbifold or 'modular-dimension-0' points of M_{0,5}/S5.

What the page is. It is an S5-equivariant census of a diagram, meaning a groupoid or 2-complex modelling M_{0,5}. Its vertices are distinguished configurations: level-0 special points plus other distinguished loci. Its arrows are of three kinds: f-arrows, tau = 'twist', and gamma = 'gommage' (erasure, apparently passing between adjacent pieces of a decomposition).

How to read each line. A line 'N = a×m = b×n  X' means the following. The arrow type X forms one S5-orbit of N arrows. Its sources form an orbit of m vertices, each emitting a arrows of type X. Its targets form an orbit of n vertices, each receiving b arrows. So N = a·m = b·n, and m, n divide 120.

Examples:
- f_{B_s}: 60 = 3×20 = 2×30. Twenty bipyramid vertices each emit three arrows to the thirty square-pyramid ('Q') vertices.
- f_{Q_a}: 120 = 4×30 = 2×60.
- gamma_{pi,s}: 60 = 1×60 = 5×12. The target is the 12 pentagon vertices, type I_10, stabiliser of order 10.
- gamma^0_r: 120 = 1×120 = 6×20.

Group totals:
- f-group: 60 + 120 = 180.
- Second group: 60 + 120 + 60 + 60 + 120 = 420. The left label is overwritten.
- Third group: 120 + 120 + 120 + 120 + 360 + 120 + 60 = 1020.
- Total: 180 + 420 + 1020 = 1620 = 5×60 + 11×120. That is 16 arrow orbits (5 of size 60, 11 of size 120), and the correction from 1380 to 1620 is consistent.

Vertices. There are said to be 542 vertices in 9 S5-orbits. One possible decomposition is 2×120 + 4×60 + 30 + 20 + 12 = 542.

Work programme.
1) Find a fundamental system of relations among the 1620 arrows, organised by S5-orbits. In particular, express every arrow as a composite of arrows 'coming from modular dimension ≤ 1'. This is the Esquisse principle that the Teichmüller tower is generated in modular dimension ≤ 1 with relations in dimension ≤ 2, here tested concretely on M_{0,5}.
2) Redo this after eliminating the level-0 vertices, keeping perhaps type I_10, the pentagon. Type II_1 reduces to type III_1, but one must watch the twist tau_{pi/6}.
3) Further eliminate the 'tetrahedral' pieces II_1, and any piece that does not simplify the presentation.

Drawings. The sketches show:
- pairs of pants and 4-holed spheres, with green dashed curves giving decompositions into elementary pieces;
- a tetrahedral piece;
- a 5-holed sphere decomposed by dashed curves;
- two spheres with 3+2 holes, the bipyramid/pyramid symmetric pictures;
- a boundary circle marked with crosses and dots, suggesting marked or tangential base points on boundary components.

Aim. The goal is an economical, symmetric, finite presentation of the orbifold fundamental groupoid of M_{0,5} (mod S5), with base points at symmetric configurations, reduced to level ≤ 1 generators.
errors: No arithmetic errors are detectable. All three group totals and the grand total 1620 = 5×60 + 11×120 check out, and the arrow-orbit count of 16 supersedes the crossed-out '14'.
The entry for tau_{pi,s} transcribed as '60 = 1×60 = 4×60' is impossible under the a×m = b×n convention. It is almost certainly '4×15', i.e. a 15-element orbit with stabiliser of order 8.
The entry for gamma^{1'}_r (3×120 = 3×120 = 3×40?) is ambiguous: 3 orbits of 120 arrows. The target side '3×40' only works if read as 3 orbits of 40 vertices, each receiving 3 arrows.

The vertex count '542' and its split into 9 orbits are not verified on the page. 542 = 2·120 + 4·60 + 30 + 20 + 12 is possible, but then orbits of size 15 or 40 suggested elsewhere would be inconsistent. Some uncertainty remains.

ideas.what: S5-equivariant combinatorial groupoid (vertices/arrows counted by orbits) modelling the fundamental groupoid of M_{0,5}, with vertices at special (symmetric) configurations
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold fundamental groupoid of M_{0,5}/S5 with base points at special loci; equivariant cell structure of M_{0,5}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Special loci and GT: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (eigenloci of 5-point configurations, early 2000s), Schneps (special loci in moduli spaces), Collas–Maugeais. Cell models: Penner, Harer, Kontsevich (ribbon graphs).
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses the Teichmüller tower, its fundamental groupoids and points of modular dimension 0, but not this explicit census.

ideas.what: Writing every arrow as a composite of arrows from modular dimension ≤1 (generation in low levels)
ideas.modern_name: Two-level principle for the Teichmüller tower (generators from level ≤1, relations from level ≤2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); proved by Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps (2000), building on Hatcher–Thurston and Moore–Seiberg

ideas.modern_name: Twist (Dehn/half-twist) moves and decomposition-change moves of Lego-Teichmüller/pants-complex type (A/S/F moves)
ideas.where_published: The Lego game is sketched in Esquisse; the 'gommage' terminology is unsure.

ideas.what: Programme of eliminating level-0 vertices and 'tetrahedral' pieces to simplify the presentation, keeping perhaps the pentagon type I_10
ideas.modern_name: Tietze-type simplification of a groupoid presentation; choice of base points at the D5-symmetric point

missed.claim: Grothendieck set up an explicit S5-equivariant presentation problem for the groupoid of M_{0,5}: 542 vertices in 9 orbits and 1620 arrows in 16 orbits (twists and 'gommages'). Base points include the special symmetric configurations (pentagon, bipyramid, square pyramid). He planned to find a complete set of relations and reduce them to level ≤1 arrows. An explicit presentation with base points at orbifold/special points, rather than tangential base points at infinity, does not appear to exist in this form.
missed.quote: déterminer un syst. fondamental de relations entre les 1620 flèches du diagramme ... en particulier, écrire toutes les flèches comme composées de flèches "provenant de la dimension modulaire ≤1"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: GT-type relations are usually derived with tangential base points (Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps). A presentation based at special points would make the action of finite automorphism groups (torsion of the mapping class group) and of Galois groups on special loci directly visible. This is relevant to the study of GT acting on special loci (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Collas–Maugeais).

missed.claim: The page and its neighbour tie the classification of special 5-point configurations, i.e. orbifold points of M_{0,5}/S5, directly to the Lego/presentation programme. The orbifold points are used as vertices of the generating groupoid, with twists by fractional angles (tau_{pi/6}) attached to them. The later 'special loci' literature arrived at this link independently, about 20 years after.
missed.quote: Reprendre les questions, en éliminant les sommets du niveau 0 (s.f. peut-être ceux de type I_10 ?) ... mais attention aux twist τ_{π/6}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a concrete hybrid presentation mixing torsion elements at special points with Lego moves. This could yield new or simpler GT relations or a symmetric presentation of the mapping class group of the 5-punctured sphere modulo S5.

deep.surprise_reason: This is mainly a bookkeeping page, but it documents a concrete, quantified S5-equivariant model of the M_{0,5} groupoid built on symmetric configurations, together with a reduction programme. That anticipates the later special-loci/GT work and is not in Esquisse in this explicit form. The underlying principles (two-level generation, Lego moves) are known and credited.
transcription_corrections: The label of the second group (crossed '180') should total 420 = 60+120+60+60+120; the overwritten figure is likely 420.
'60 = 1×60 = 4×60' for tau_{pi,s} should almost certainly read '60 = 1×60 = 4×15'.
'en partageant entre 14 orbites' is crossed out; by the page's own count there are 16 arrow orbits (5 of size 60, 11 of size 120).
'G_K' / '𝔖_K' denotes the symmetric group on the 5-element set K (order 120), consistent with all orbit sizes dividing 120.
The crossed '[-τ_ρ-]' on the third line of the 1020 group is followed by 'τ_r'; the line reads '120 = 1×120 = 2×60  τ_r'.
'f_{B_s}' and 'f_{Q_a}' probably refer to the bipyramid (B, orbit 20) and square-pyramid/quadrilateral (Q, orbit 30) special configurations of page 33.
